title: WSDG: retire Visual Studio 2019 for VS2022

notes.body: VS2019 will continue to work for now though?

Nothing has changed on the back end. I rebuild my Windows VM every 9 months and (mostly) follow the steps in the WSDG to see what might have changed to trip up someone that is new to the build process.  
  
The current stable (4.0.1) and development (4.1.0rc0) builds are using VS2022 so it was confusing to have VS2019 mentions in the WSDG.  

The compiler appears to be the same version in VS2019 and VS2022.

As noted, we should probably mention that we still support VS 2019, but the change looks good to me otherwise.

We require Visual Studio 2019 version 16.8 or later in CMakeLists.txt, so we should probably add back something like

    If you prefer you can instead download and install https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/thank-you-downloading-visual-studio/?sku=Community&rel=16[“Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 Community Edition”].
    The examples below are for Visual Studio 2022 but can be adapted for Visual Studio 2019.
